summary: Used this turn for an independent lead found while tracing ownership, rather than a close-out. New finding, source-settled with no execution needed: the actor layer takes the core instance away from the caller and offers no compaction path. spawn_actor::<T, B, R>(op: OmniPaxos<T, B>, cfg) consumes the instance by value (handle.rs:295); the handle it returns carries only cmd_tx, events_rx, outgoing_rx, incoming_tx and a channel capacity, with no accessor back; the client protocol has no compaction request (Command is Append, AppendNotify, CurrentLeader, DecidedIdx, ReadDecidedSuffix, SubscribeDecided, Reconfigure, TryBecomeLeader, Reconnected — event.rs:90-128); and the actor never calls op.trim()/op.snapshot() (its only 'trim' is trim_oldest over its own outgoing buffer, actor.rs:239/715-720). Meanwhile the core documents compaction as a user operation on the instance (trim and snapshot, omni_paxos.rs:242-262) and the layer's own docs present it as the way to run the core without driving it (lib.rs:7-15), with the shipped example using only the handle. So a runtime-only user cannot bound the log's growth: an omitted operation of the layer that owns the instance, operational rather than safety- or liveness-critical, with the three inspected places named and the limits recorded (no documented claim of feature parity; the storage backend's fill-up behaviour not examined; the same handle does expose other core-facing operations, so it is a specific omission). I also corrected two prose inaccuracies I had introduced (the enum's real line range, and an unverified method name in the comparison list). Standing position unchanged: the event-backpressure finding (capacities 8/64/1024, cluster stall, corrected transport, timescale bound 21.69s), the core's missing accept-phase repair for a lost Accepted (2-node scope), and append_notify's false Ok for an unadopted index with the adopted-vs-unadopted boundary measured.
